Recipe: Vegan Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_006)
Section: Allergen Note

Contains no fish, no shellfish, no dairy, no egg, no nuts and no gluten. Tamari is used specifically in place of ordinary soy sauce because ordinary soy sauce is brewed with wheat. Suitable for vegans and vegetarians.

Recipe: Vegan Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_006)
Section: Ingredients

Percentages are calculated against the 2000 g of prepared napa cabbage. The salted shrimp and anchovy fish sauce of the traditional card are replaced here by a shiitake and kombu umami base.

| Ingredient | Weight | Percentage of cabbage |
|---|---|---|
| Napa cabbage | 2000 g | 100% |
| Coarse sea salt (for brining) | 160 g | 8% |
| Gochugaru (Korean chilli flakes) | 100 g | 5% |
| Korean radish, julienned | 400 g | 20% |
| Garlic, minced | 60 g | 3% |
| Ginger, grated | 20 g | 1% |
| Dried shiitake mushrooms | 30 g | 1.5% |
| Kombu (dried kelp) | 10 g | 0.5% |
| Tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) | 50 g | 2.5% |
| Glutinous rice flour | 30 g | 1.5% |
| Caster sugar | 20 g | 1% |

Recipe: Vegan Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_006)
Section: Ingredients

Total yield is approximately 2.85 kg of finished kimchi.

Recipe: Vegan Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_006)
Section: Method

Brine the quartered cabbage with the full 160 g of coarse sea salt for 4 to 6 hours, turning every 2 hours, then apply the bend test: a thick white stem should bend into a U without snapping. Rinse three times and drain cut side down for one hour.

Build the umami base while the cabbage brines. Simmer the dried shiitake and the kombu in 400 ml of water for 20 minutes, then remove the kombu before it turns slimy and simmer the shiitake for a further 10 minutes. Strain, reserving 250 ml of the liquid, and finely chop the rehydrated shiitake caps to fold into the paste.

Recipe: Vegan Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_006)
Section: Method

This shiitake and kombu stock plus the tamari is what replaces the saeujeot and anchovy fish sauce used on the traditional card. Both supply glutamates, which is the savoury depth the fermented seafood would otherwise provide.

Whisk the glutinous rice flour into the reserved 250 ml of mushroom stock, heat gently for 5 minutes until thickened, stir in the sugar and cool completely.

Mix the cooled porridge with the gochugaru and rest for 10 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, chopped shiitake and tamari. Fold through the julienned radish.

Coat every leaf with the paste, pack into a jar with 5 cm of headspace, and press down until the brine rises above the cabbage.

Recipe: Vegan Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_006)
Section: Method

Ferment at 20C for 2 to 3 days, which is around a day longer than the traditional card requires because the seafood ferments in saeujeot give the traditional version a head start. Move to the refrigerator once bubbling and pleasantly sour.

Recipe: 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf (recipe_id: ferment_001)
Section: Allergen Note

Contains wheat and rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains no dairy, no egg and no nuts. Suitable for vegans. Produced in a bakery that also handles milk, egg and sesame.

Recipe: 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf (recipe_id: ferment_001)
Section: Ingredients

Total flour weight is 2000 g and all baker's percentages below are calculated against that total flour weight. Final hydration is 80%.

| Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % |
|---|---|---|
| Strong white bread flour | 1700 g | 85% |
| Wholemeal flour | 300 g | 15% |
| Water (28C) | 1600 g | 80% |
| Fine sea salt | 40 g | 2% |
| Rye levain (100% hydration) | 400 g | 20% |

Recipe: 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf (recipe_id: ferment_001)
Section: Ingredients

Total dough weight is 4040 g, which divides into two loaves of roughly 2020 g each.

Recipe: 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf (recipe_id: ferment_001)
Section: Method

Autolyse first. Combine the strong white flour, the wholemeal flour and 1500 g of the water in a large tub, mixing until no dry flour remains, then cover and rest for 60 minutes. Hold back the remaining 100 g of water for the salt stage.

Add the rye levain and squeeze it through the dough until fully dispersed. Rest for 30 minutes.

Now add the fine sea salt together with the reserved 100 g of water. The salt goes in after the autolyse and after the levain, never at the start, because salt tightens the gluten network and slows the enzymatic activity the autolyse is meant to encourage. Squeeze and fold until the dough feels smooth and no grittiness remains at the base of the tub.

Recipe: 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf (recipe_id: ferment_001)
Section: Method

Bulk ferment for 4 to 5 hours at 24C, performing a set of coil folds every 45 minutes for the first three hours. The bulk is finished when the dough has risen by roughly 50%, feels aerated, and shows a domed surface with visible bubbles at the edge of the tub.

Divide into two pieces, pre-shape lightly and bench rest for 25 minutes. Shape into boules, place seam side up in floured bannetons, and cold retard in the refrigerator at 4C for 12 to 16 hours.

Bake straight from the refrigerator in a preheated cast iron combo cooker. Bake at 250C for 20 minutes with the lid on, then remove the lid, drop the oven to 230C and bake for a further 25 minutes until the crust is deep brown and the internal temperature reaches 96C.

Recipe: 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf (recipe_id: ferment_001)
Section: Method

Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before cutting.

Recipe: Rye Levain Starter (recipe_id: ferment_002)
Section: Allergen Note

Contains rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains no dairy, no egg and no nuts. Suitable for vegans.

Recipe: Rye Levain Starter (recipe_id: ferment_002)
Section: Ingredients

This is a 100% hydration levain, meaning the water weight equals the flour weight. Baker's percentages are calculated against the 100 g of rye flour.

| Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % |
|---|---|---|
| Wholegrain rye flour | 100 g | 100% |
| Water (26C) | 100 g | 100% |
| Mature sourdough starter | 20 g | 20% |

Recipe: Rye Levain Starter (recipe_id: ferment_002)
Section: Ingredients

Total levain yield is 220 g, which is enough to build the 400 g of levain required by the 2kg Country Sourdough after one further refreshment.

Recipe: Rye Levain Starter (recipe_id: ferment_002)
Section: Method

Weigh the mature starter into a clear straight-sided jar and mark the level with an elastic band so the rise can be judged by eye rather than by guesswork.

Add the water at 26C and stir until the starter is dispersed and the liquid turns cloudy. Add the wholegrain rye flour and mix to a thick paste. Rye holds far more water than white flour, so at 100% hydration this will look like a stiff batter rather than a dough.

Recipe: Rye Levain Starter (recipe_id: ferment_002)
Section: Method

Cover loosely and ferment for 8 to 12 hours at 22 to 24C. The levain is ripe when it has at least doubled from the elastic band mark, the surface is domed and covered in fine bubbles, and it smells sharply sour with a faint acetone note. A levain that has risen and then collapsed back to a flat, watery surface has gone past ripe and will give a slack, over-acidified dough.

The float test is a useful confirmation: drop a teaspoon of ripe levain into room temperature water and it should float rather than sink.

Refresh at least once every 24 hours if the starter is kept at room temperature, or once a week if it is stored at 4C in the refrigerator.

Section: Allergen Note

Contains wheat and rye, therefore contains gluten. Contains no dairy, no egg and no nuts. Suitable for vegans.

Section: Ingredients

Baker's percentages are calculated against the 1000 g of strong white flour. Final hydration is 85%.

| Ingredient | Weight | Baker's % |
|---|---|---|
| Strong white bread flour | 1000 g | 100% |
| Water (24C) | 850 g | 85% |
| Rye levain (100% hydration) | 250 g | 25% |
| Fine sea salt | 22 g | 2.2% |
| Extra virgin olive oil | 60 g | 6% |

Recipe: Sourdough Focaccia (recipe_id: ferment_003)
Section: Ingredients

Total dough weight is 2182 g, which fills one 30 x 40 cm tray.

Recipe: Sourdough Focaccia (recipe_id: ferment_003)
Section: Method

Mix the flour and 800 g of the water until no dry flour remains and rest for 45 minutes. Reserve the last 50 g of water for the salt.

Add the levain and mix through, then rest 30 minutes. Add the fine sea salt with the reserved water and squeeze until fully incorporated. Finally drizzle in the olive oil and work it in. The dough will look broken and greasy at first and will come back together after two minutes of folding.

Bulk ferment for 3 to 4 hours at 24C with four sets of coil folds spaced 30 minutes apart. At 85% hydration the dough is slack, so use a wet hand and lift rather than stretch.

Recipe: Sourdough Focaccia (recipe_id: ferment_003)
Section: Method

Oil the tray generously, tip the dough in without deflating it, and spread it gently towards the corners. If it springs back, wait 20 minutes and try again rather than forcing it. Cold retard in the refrigerator for 12 hours.

Bring the tray to room temperature for 90 minutes before baking. Dimple the surface firmly with oiled fingertips, pressing all the way down to the tray so the dough does not dome, then drizzle with a further tablespoon of olive oil and scatter with flaky salt.

Bake at 240C for 22 minutes until the top is deep golden and the underside is crisp when lifted with a spatula. Lift the focaccia straight out of the tray onto a rack so the base does not steam.

runs.answer:
**Sourdough Focaccia (recipe_id = ferment_003)**  

**Ingredients**  
- Strong white bread flour – 1000 g (100 % baker’s %).  
- Water (24 °C) – 850 g (85 % baker’s %).  
- Rye levain (100 % hydration) – 250 g (25 % baker’s %).  
- Fine sea salt – 22 g (2.2 % baker’s %).  
- Extra‑virgin olive oil – 60 g (6 % baker’s %).  

*Total dough weight: 2182 g, enough for one 30 × 40 cm tray*【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__ingredients__1 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

**Method**  

1. **Mix & autolyse** – Combine the flour and 800 g of the water; mix until no dry flour remains. Rest 45 minutes. Reserve the remaining 50 g water for later【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__0 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

2. **Add levain** – Incorporate the rye levain and mix through. Rest 30 minutes【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__0 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

3. **Add salt** – Dissolve the fine sea salt in the reserved 50 g water and squeeze it into the dough until fully incorporated【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__0 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

4. **Add oil** – Drizzle the olive oil into the dough and work it in; the dough will look broken and greasy at first, then come together after a couple of folds【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__0 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

5. **Bulk ferment** – Let the dough ferment 3–4 hours at 24 °C, performing four sets of coil folds spaced 30 minutes apart. Use wet hands to handle the slack, 85 % hydration dough【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__0 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

6. **Shape & pre‑proof** – Oil a 30 × 40 cm tray generously. Tip the dough in without deflating it and gently spread toward the corners. If the dough springs back, wait 20 minutes and try again.  

7. **Cold retard** – Refrigerate the tray for 12 hours【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__1 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

8. **Bring to room temperature** – Let the tray sit at room temperature for 90 minutes before baking.  

9. **Dimple & finish** – Dimple the surface firmly with oiled fingertips, pressing down to the tray so the dough does not dome. Drizzle a further tablespoon of olive oil over the top and scatter flaky salt【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__1 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.  

10. **Bake** – Bake at 240 °C for 22 minutes, until the top is deep golden and the underside is crisp when lifted with a spatula.  

11. **Cool** – Lift the focaccia straight out of the tray onto a rack so the base does not steam【recipe_id=ferment_003 | chunk_id=ferment_003__method__1 | source_file=ferment_003_sourdough_focaccia.md】.

Bake at 240C for 22 minutes until the top is deep golden and the underside is crisp when lifted with a spatula. Lift the focaccia straight out of the tray onto a rack so the base does not steam.

Recipe: Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_005)
Section: Allergen Note

Contains fish in the form of anchovy fish sauce and contains crustacean shellfish in the form of salted fermented shrimp. Not suitable for vegetarians or vegans. Contains no dairy, no egg, no nuts and no gluten. Despite its name, glutinous rice flour contains no gluten.

Recipe: Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_005)
Section: Ingredients

Percentages here are calculated against the 2000 g of prepared napa cabbage rather than against flour, since this is a vegetable ferment rather than a dough.

| Ingredient | Weight | Percentage of cabbage |
|---|---|---|
| Napa cabbage | 2000 g | 100% |
| Coarse sea salt (for brining) | 160 g | 8% |
| Gochugaru (Korean chilli flakes) | 100 g | 5% |
| Korean radish, julienned | 400 g | 20% |
| Garlic, minced | 60 g | 3% |
| Ginger, grated | 20 g | 1% |
| Saeujeot (salted fermented shrimp) | 60 g | 3% |
| Anchovy fish sauce | 60 g | 3% |
| Glutinous rice flour | 30 g | 1.5% |
| Caster sugar | 20 g | 1% |

Recipe: Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_005)
Section: Ingredients

Total yield is approximately 2.9 kg of finished kimchi.

Recipe: Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_005)
Section: Method

Quarter the cabbage lengthwise keeping the core attached, then brine it using the full 160 g of coarse sea salt, working the salt between the leaves and concentrating it on the thick white stems. Leave for 4 to 6 hours, turning every 2 hours.

The cabbage is correctly brined when a thick white stem bends into a U shape without snapping. This bend test matters more than the clock, because cabbage size and moisture content vary considerably between heads.

Rinse three times in cold water and drain cut side down for at least one hour. Residual water dilutes the paste and can spoil the ferment.

Recipe: Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_005)
Section: Method

Make the rice porridge by whisking the glutinous rice flour into 250 ml of cold water, heating gently for 5 minutes until it thickens, then stirring in the sugar and cooling completely. The porridge feeds the lactobacillus and speeds the early fermentation.

Combine the cooled porridge with the gochugaru and let it stand for 10 minutes so the chilli flakes bloom, then mix in the garlic, ginger, saeujeot and anchovy fish sauce. Fold through the julienned radish.

Wearing gloves, spread the paste over every leaf, working from the stem end outward. Pack into a jar, pressing down firmly to eliminate air pockets, and leave 5 cm of headspace.

Recipe: Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_005)
Section: Method

Ferment at 20C for 2 days until bubbles appear and the smell turns sour, then transfer to the refrigerator at 4C. The kimchi is edible immediately but reaches its best flavour after 2 weeks.
